name: upgrade
body:
Upgrade surface: the `kalide upgrade` command and the in-place migration it performs — detect a deck (`kalide.yaml`) or a template library (`library.yaml`) via `detectProject`, decide per kalide-owned file whether to refresh it (present and byte-identical to a known released kalide version in the embedded digest catalogue, or an absent `AGENTS.md` author guide), apply the ordered format migrations defined for the project's version, validate the result, and report every refreshed and every left-alone path.

The `internal/cli` handler `runUpgrade` (internal/cli/upgrade.go) accepts no argument and no `--force`, resolves the current directory with `os.Getwd`, and turns scaffold's outcome into the exit code and user-facing text: success prints the `UpgradeReport` (refreshed and skipped paths) and exits 0; a both/neither project, an unsupported library format, or a failed end-to-end validation prints scaffold's message to stderr and exits 1; any argument is a usage error (exit 2). `cli.Run` dispatches the `upgrade` case to it, beside init, init-library, start, templates, version and help; that shared dispatcher is owned by solution.component.cli-commands.

The `internal/scaffold` entry point `Upgrade` (internal/scaffold/upgrade.go) orchestrates the two halves: detection through `detectProject` and a read-only format guard (`checkSupportedLibraryFormat`) before any write; the never-clobber refresh half `refreshScaffold` (with `refreshReport.refreshMember`/`writeMember` and the seed-vs-external-library predicate `detectSeedDeck`) in internal/scaffold/refresh.go; and the ordered, versioned migration half `migrateLibrary` → `runMigrations` over `registeredMigrations` in internal/scaffold/migrate.go. It then validates the result end-to-end through the same loaders `kalide start` uses. An all-or-nothing undo (a whole-tree snapshot for a library, recorded original bytes for the refresh writes) restores the project exactly on failure. The refresh half identifies known versions through the embedded digest catalogue in internal/scaffold/catalog.go (`catalogLookup`); it reuses the embedded author guides and init seed content. The command is local-filesystem only, offline, with no `--force`.
